changelog: - **e2e: a rate-limit flood no longer spends everybody else's bucket, and CI now says so before the scheduled run does** (#2159, #2158). `enforceRateLimit` keys on `bucket:ip` into a per-process store, and a full-suite shard runs its whole file list against one Next server (`workers: 1`, one `webServer`) — so every request that arrives without a usable client address counts into the same `<bucket>:unknown` counter, the suite's calls to an endpoint are cumulative, and the windows are 10-60 minutes, longer than a shard takes. `rate-limit.spec.ts`'s six POSTs to `/api/support` (limit 5) therefore left `support-attachments.spec.ts` and `support-chat.spec.ts` with nothing to spend and pinned shard 4/4 of `e2e-full` red on the same two tests every non-skipped run; `mentor-applications.spec.ts` was at exactly 5/5 on its own and handed the 429 to whatever ran next. New `e2e/helpers/rateLimit.ts` hands out synthetic `X-Real-IP` addresses — `floodIp()` a stable one for a test that is *measuring* the brake and must spend one counter repeatedly, `freshIp()` a new one per call for a spec that merely has to drive a rate-limited endpoint to reach the feature behind it. It goes through `x-real-ip` rather than `X-Forwarded-For` precisely because the webServer runs with `TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT=0` so the #858 spoofing test can prove a rotating forwarded header buys nothing — that test keeps the address it did not choose, since sharing is its whole claim. `support-chat.spec.ts` alone posts seven support messages against a limit of five, so a per-spec budget would only have moved the cliff. Browser-driven sends are covered too (`extraHTTPHeaders` on the context, `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders` on the default fixture). The class is closed rather than the instances: `npm run check:e2e-rate-limits` (new, in `ci.yml`) reads every bucket's limit and window straight out of the route files and counts the unisolated e2e call sites that spend it — cumulatively for a window longer than five minutes, per spec file for a shorter one, skipping buckets keyed on a `subject:` rather than an IP — and fails the PR when a bucket is within reach. It found `register` sitting at 13/15 before anything was red; those thirteen call sites are isolated here too. No product code changes: the limiter is unchanged and still asserted.
